title: Effective Cartier divisors are nowhere dense
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $D\subseteq X$ be the closed subscheme cut out by an effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal I_D\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Then the open complement $U=X\setminus D$, with inclusion $j:U\to X$, is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open], i.e. $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. In particular its underlying topological space is dense, so $D$ contains no nonempty open subset of $X$.

source.place: Tag 07ZU (Divisors, Lemma effective Cartier complement is affine and scheme-theoretically dense)

proof.text: By [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], $\mathcal I_D$ has, on the members of an open cover, a generator which is a non-zero-divisor in the ring of sections of that member; as in the Stacks proof we take these members affine, $W=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ with generator $b\in B$. Refining further by principal affine opens $V=D(g)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_g)$ of such a $W$ keeps the generator regular: $B\to B_g$ is a localization, so by [lem-pc-localization-preserves-nonzerodivisor] the image $a$ of $b$ in $A=B_g$ is a non-zero-divisor, and $\mathcal I_D|_V$ is generated by $a$. Thus $X$ has an affine open cover by charts $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ on which $\mathcal I_D$ is generated by a non-zero-divisor $a\in A$, and on each such chart $U\cap V=D(a)$.

source.place: Tag 07ZU, proof using Lemma characterize-effective-Cartier-divisor and affine localization

proof.text: On each affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, the open immersion $j|_{U\cap V}:D(a)\to V$ is affine, hence quasi-compact. By [lem-pc-affine-nonzerodivisor-complement-dense], $\mathcal O_V\to (j|_{U\cap V})_*\mathcal O_{U\cap V}$ is injective and $U\cap V$ is topologically dense in $V$.

source.place: Tag 07ZU, proof: $A\subset A_a$ for a nonzerodivisor $a$

proof.text: The quasi-compactness checks on the affine cover imply that $j:U\to X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target]. Injectivity of $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is local on the target, so the affine checks give this injectivity globally. Since every affine chart meets $U$ densely, $U$ is topologically dense in $X$; therefore $D$ contains no nonempty open subset. The injectivity is exactly the scheme-theoretic density predicate [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open].
